title: Multiplication image of two finite type quasi-coherent algebra subsheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $\mathcal A$ be a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf] whose underlying module is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\mathcal B_1,\mathcal B_2\subseteq\mathcal A$ be quasi-coherent algebra subsheaves of finite type, meaning $\mathcal B_k(U)$ is a finitely generated $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra for every affine open $U$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-quasi-coherent-subalgebras]. There is a unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\mu:\mathcal B_1\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal B_2\to\mathcal A$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] whose composite with the presheaf-to-sheaf tensor map sends $b_1\otimes b_2$ to $b_1b_2$ on every open. Define $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal A$ to be its sheaf image: $\mathcal C(W)$ consists of sections of $\mathcal A(W)$ locally in the image of $\mu$. Then $\mathcal C$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-subalgebra of finite type containing both $\mathcal B_1$ and $\mathcal B_2$. For every affine open $U$, with $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $\mathcal C(U)$ is the image of $\mathcal B_1(U)\otimes_R\mathcal B_2(U)\to\mathcal A(U)$, $b_1\otimes b_2\mapsto b_1b_2$, and is the $R$-subalgebra generated by $\mathcal B_1(U)\cup\mathcal B_2(U)$. In particular, if finite lists $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ and $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ generate $\mathcal B_1(U)$ and $\mathcal B_2(U)$ as $R$-algebras, their combined list generates $\mathcal C(U)$.

proof.text: On every open, multiply the images of sections of the two algebra subsheaves in the ambient algebra. The underlying-module functor [def-weil-pbc-ringed-space-algebra-module] identifies their scalar actions. Distributivity and commutativity prove bilinearity, and restriction maps preserve multiplication. Apply the proved sheaf tensor bilinear universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] to this natural family. Its pure-tensor equation is the required formula for the canonical tensorSectionsMap, and its uniqueness clause gives uniqueness of the multiplication morphism. This implements the tensor and sheafification construction [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] without repeating its universal-property proof.

proof.text: The modules underlying $\mathcal B_1$ and $\mathcal B_2$ are quasi-coherent by hypothesis. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections] gives quasi-coherence of $\mathcal T$ and bijectivity of the canonical $t_U$ on every affine open $U$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] to $\mu$, whose target $\mathcal A$ is also quasi-coherent by hypothesis. Its locally defined image is exactly the specified $\mathcal C$; hence $\mathcal C$ is a quasi-coherent submodule sheaf and $\mathcal C(U)=\mu_U(\mathcal T(U))$ for affine $U$. Since $\mu_U t_U=\nu_U$ by Step 1 and $t_U$ is surjective, $\mathcal C(U)=\nu_U(\mathcal B_1(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\mathcal B_2(U))$, proving the claimed affine image formula.

source.place: Tag 05JT (lemma-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-type), proof, first paragraph: multiplication image; details omitted there supplied explicitly. Underlying sheaf facts are Schemes Tags 01I8 (lemma-widetilde-constructions), 01IB (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent), 01IC (lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent), and 01LA (section-quasi-coherent).

proof.text: Fix affine $U$ and put $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$. By pure-tensor generation [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], the image in Step 2 consists of finite sums $\sum_i b_i c_i$ with $b_i\in\mathcal B_1(U)$ and $c_i\in\mathcal B_2(U)$; coefficients in $R$ can be absorbed into $b_i$. It contains $b=b\cdot1$, $c=1\cdot c$, and the image of every scalar $r=r\cdot1$. Products remain in it because $(\sum_i b_i c_i)(\sum_j b'_j c'_j)=\sum_{i,j}(b_i b'_j)(c_i c'_j)$; additive inverses and sums remain in it by the submodule property. Thus $\mathcal C(U)$ is an $R$-subalgebra containing both section algebras. Every $R$-subalgebra containing them contains each such sum, so $\mathcal C(U)$ is exactly their generated subalgebra. For arbitrary open $W$, use [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] to cover $W$ by affine opens contained in $W$. For $s,t\in\mathcal C(W)$, their restrictions to each such affine $U$ lie in $\mathcal C(U)$, so $st|_U\in\mathcal C(U)$ by the affine calculation. Also $1|_U\in\mathcal C(U)$. These local sections agree on overlaps as sections of $\mathcal A$, and hence of its subsheaf $\mathcal C$. The sheaf property from Step 2 gives $st,1\in\mathcal C(W)$. The same argument applied to a section of either $\mathcal B_k(W)$ shows it lies in $\mathcal C(W)$. The inherited operations and restrictions consequently make $\mathcal C$ an $\mathcal O_X$-subalgebra sheaf containing both $\mathcal B_k$. In Lean, construct the ring presheaf explicitly as these sectionwise subrings, with restrictions inherited from the ambient algebra. Its underlying presheaf is isomorphic to the module image by the injective image inclusion and equality of section ranges, hence is a sheaf. Transport the module image quasi-coherence through this isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-ringed-space-algebra-module]. Factor both original algebra inclusions through the constructed subalgebra by their sectionwise ranges, then use the canonical representative of its categorical subobject; the representative is isomorphic to the constructed subalgebra, so all range and quasi-coherence assertions transfer.

proof.text: On affine $U$, let $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ and $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ be the finite algebra generators in the statement. The $R$-subalgebra $D$ of $\mathcal A(U)$ generated by their combined list is contained in $\mathcal C(U)$ by Step 3. Conversely $D$ contains each $\mathcal B_k(U)$, since every element of the first is a polynomial in the $x_i$ over $R$ and every element of the second is a polynomial in the $y_j$. Step 3 then gives $\mathcal C(U)\subseteq D$. Thus the combined list generates $\mathcal C(U)$. Such finite lists exist on every affine $U$ by the finite type hypotheses. Together with quasi-coherence from Step 2 and the algebra-subsheaf property from Step 3, this is exactly finite type in [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-quasi-coherent-subalgebras].
